rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so the ceiling is obfuscation strength, not robustness; this program is a tiny (2-function, ~512B text) numeric Shootout kernel whose entire execution lives in one hot loop inside main, so the strategy is to lean hard on passes whose transformations are cheap per-execution and apply them aggressively — SUB (arithmetic substitution, near-free for integer matrix math), SPLIT (basic-block splitting, negligible cost but high diversity), and ICALL/IGV (indirect calls and global variable indirection, which destroy static call/data-flow recovery in a program with so few functions that every remaining landmark is valuable). FLA and BCF were previously the correct things to hold back and stay held back: their loop-unrolling and opaque-predicate bloating land directly in the hot loop and would blow the runtime budget on a benchmark defined by its execution speed, so their RuntimeCost weights remain low (0.15-0.25) to keep them from binding here. IBR gets a moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.45) because indirect branching is high-value against a disassembler in a program this small but does add per-block cost in the hot path. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low across the board since round 0 showed no fragility, giving the selector room to compose multiple passes per function without risking the build.
